intro.TrustedMarkup:
The untyped half of fromJson, and the generator of the typed half.

jsonDecoders writes the typed half per target type. What it writes reads the source once through a JsonReader and decodes each value into its slot; it builds no Json tree. It calls this module for the reader, Issues, paths and scalar decoders. Decoding accumulates: a decoder records its failure and returns, and a composite constructs only when every part succeeded. So every decoder returns an Array<T> of zero or one element; empty means the issue is already recorded. Option<T> cannot serve: with T = Option<U> it has no wire form. Every message is the canonical wording, byte for byte. A refused document yields its json.parse Issue alone, and a record's Issues follow its members' declaration order, whatever the document's key order.

The tree accessors (fieldsOf, fieldAt and the rest) serve programs that read a Json from parseJson.

prose.TrustedMarkup: A bare string's content (a nullary enum variant's wire form), or "". No variant can be named "", so the sentinel cannot collide with a real tag.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn pathAt(path: String, seg: String, idx: Int64) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: The path of a value a decoder reads: path itself when idx is -2, path[idx] for an element, and path.seg for a member when idx is -1. A decoder builds it only for an Issue or for its own members, so a value that decodes builds no path.

fn dInt64(p: modify JsonReader, path: String, seg: String, idx: Int64, iss: modify Array<Issue>) -> Array<Int64>

prose.TrustedMarkup: A JSON integer-syntax number as an exact Int64. A fraction, an exponent or a magnitude outside Int64 is expected integer, never a rounded value.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn dIntKey(key: String, path: String, iss: modify Array<Issue>) -> Array<Int64>

prose.TrustedMarkup: An object key read as an Int64, the wire form of Map<Int64, V>, in the map at path. Only the canonical text (n.toString()) passes: "007" and "+7" would otherwise collapse into the key "7" with no Issue.

prose.TrustedMarkup: dInt64 restricted to [lo, hi], for the sized signed integers.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn dUIntMax( p: modify JsonReader, path: String, seg: String, idx: Int64, iss: modify Array<Issue>, hi: UInt64, ) -> Array<UInt64>

prose.TrustedMarkup: A JSON integer-syntax number as an exact UInt64 in [0, hi]. parseInt64 cannot serve: it has no room above Int64.max.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn dFloat64(p: modify JsonReader, path: String, seg: String, idx: Int64, iss: modify Array<Issue>) -> Array<Float64>

prose.TrustedMarkup: A JSON number as a Float64, correctly rounded (std/num). Integer syntax is accepted: 1 decodes into a Float64 target as 1.0.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn dFloat32(p: modify JsonReader, path: String, seg: String, idx: Int64, iss: modify Array<Issue>) -> Array<Float32>

prose.TrustedMarkup: A JSON number as a Float32, rounded once: decimal -> Float64 -> Float32 rounds twice and is wrong near a Float32 tie.

sig.TrustedMarkup: gen fn jsonDecoders(t: TypeArg) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: Writes the decoders fromJson calls: for each root, the entry that reads a document into Validation<T>, and for each node, the function that decodes the value at a reader's cursor into zero or one value. Generated source cannot spell reserved names, so it writes VyrnRt_ for std/json's, VyrnRd_ for this module's and VyrnWp_ for a where type's predicate.
